name: DocIQ
description: Document image quality assessment (DIQA) is an important component for various applications, including optical character recognition (OCR), document restoration, and the evaluation of enhancement systems. We introduce DIQA-5000, a subjective dataset of 5,000 enhanced document images generated by applying diverse enhancement pipelines to 500 real-world captures with common distortions including blur, shadow, occlusion, creases, and moiré. Each enhanced image was rated by 15 subjects across three perceptual dimensions: overall quality, sharpness, and color fidelity. To address the absence of document-specialized no-reference IQA models, we propose DocIQ, which combines layout-aware downsampling with a multi-level feature fusion module to effectively capture both structural and semantic quality cues. Our architecture employs independent, dimension-specific regression heads to model rater variability and jointly predict multi-dimensional scores from a single input. Experiments demonstrate that DocIQ outperforms state-of-the-art general-purpose IQA methods on both DIQA-5000 and the OCR-based SmartDoc-QA benchmark.
